assessments.reasoning: The SPDX license-list-data repository's annotated tag object 76c9a79bb7d2bf851143b76b3935a4d7cbaa644b names v3.29.0 and targets an object of type commit with SHA 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48. That is the commit used to retrieve the BY detail. The API reports the tag as unsigned.

At that commit, json/details/DL-DE-BY-2.0.json records the exact key, English name, isDeprecatedLicenseId=false, and https://www.govdata.de/dl-de/by-2-0 in crossRef and seeAlso. The German and English clauses identify the attribution edition independently of the filename.

The pinned municipal copy supplies the publisher-side context. Its named HTTPS link matches the SPDX reference, and its attribution provisions distinguish the edition. Frankfurt's page establishes what the city published, while SPDX supplies list membership.

GovData's own BY article connects the German title, short designation and identical HTTPS path. Its explicit treatment of Zero as an alternative resolves a plausible family-name collision. Its copied passages provide contextual edition evidence only.

limitations: SPDX cites GovData directly. Its detail contains no direct citation to Frankfurt. The shared URL supports the edition link without establishing the bytes served by that URL today.

The tag is unsigned. The finding concerns the repository's annotated tag object and generated JSON. XML build lineage, verbatim equivalence, work-specific grants and Index admission require other evidence.
reasoning: SPDX assigns DL-DE-BY-2.0 to “Data licence Germany – attribution – version 2.0” in the generated license detail at the commit targeted by v3.29.0. The detail names GovData's BY route. Frankfurt's copy identifies that same route and edition, and GovData's own documentation confirms the association. This satisfies SCES §7's requirement to pin an external assertion to its owning index and release. The correspondence to Frankfurt's copy follows from comparing the evidence on both sides.
